title: Binary trees & depth-first traversals
overview: This module starts trees. You build a small binary tree by hand with `Node` objects that have `left` and `right` pointers, then visit every node with the three depth-first orders: pre-order, in-order and post-order. The three orders are the same recursion with the print moved to a different place.

concepts.explain: Each node stores a value and two pointers, `left` and `right`. A missing child is `NULL`. The top node is the **root**; a node with no children is a **leaf**.
concepts.snippet: class Node { public: int val; Node* left; Node* right; };

concepts.explain: Create nodes with `new Node(x)` and connect them by assigning `root->left = a;` and so on. You reach deeper nodes by chaining arrows, like `root->right->left`.
A tree is a root plus a left subtree plus a right subtree. So a function can handle the root and call itself on the two subtrees. The base case is `root == NULL`: nothing to do.
Print the node first, then visit left, then right. The root always comes first in the output.
Visit the whole left subtree, then print the node, then the right subtree. The root ends up in the middle.
Visit both subtrees first and print the node last. The root always comes last, which is handy when children must be handled before parents (for example, deleting a tree).

files.title: Build a binary tree by hand
files.what: Creates six nodes and links them into a tree: 10 is the root, 20 and 30 are its children, 40 hangs under 20, and 50, 60 hang under 30. Then it prints each value by walking the pointers.
steps: `Node(int val)` sets the value and makes `left` and `right` `NULL`.
Links: `root->left = a`, `root->right = b`, `a->left = c`, `b->left = d`, `b->right = e`.
Each `cout` reaches a node from the root, e.g. `root->right->left->val` is 50.
files.output_note: Six lines, 10 to 60, confirming each pointer path reaches the node you expected.
files.watch_out: Reading `root->left->right->val` here would crash: `a->right` is `NULL`. Always know a child exists before following it.

check.q: Which nodes are leaves in this tree?

files.title: Pre-order traversal
files.what: Same hand-built tree, plus a recursive `preorder` that prints Root, then Left subtree, then Right subtree.
steps: Then it calls `preorder(root->left)` and finishes that whole side.
For our tree: 10, then left side (20, 40), then right side (30, 50, 60).
files.complexity: Time O(n) · Space O(h) for the call stack (h = height)
files.output_note: After the six value lines: `Pre-order traversal: 10 20 40 30 50 60`. The root 10 is first.

check.q: In pre-order, which value is always printed first?

files.title: In-order traversal
files.what: Adds `inorder`, which prints Left subtree, then Root, then Right subtree, and prints both pre-order and in-order.
steps: It first calls `inorder(root->left)` so the entire left side prints.
files.output_note: The last line reads `Pre-order traversal: 10 20 40 30 50 60 In-order traversal: 40 20 10 50 30 60` — both on one line.
files.watch_out: There is no `endl` after `preorder(root)`, so the two traversals run together on one line. Add `cout << endl;` after each call to separate them.

check.q: Where does the root 10 appear in the in-order output, and why?
check.a: In the middle (after 40 20), because the whole left subtree is printed before the root.

files.title: Post-order traversal
files.what: Adds `postorder`, which prints Left subtree, then Right subtree, then Root, and prints all three orders.
steps: Only after both children are done does it print `root->val`.
For our tree: 40 20 (left side), 50 60 30 (right side), then 10.
files.output_note: The last line holds all three: pre-order `10 20 40 30 50 60`, in-order `40 20 10 50 30 60`, post-order `40 20 50 60 30 10`.
files.watch_out: Same missing `endl` as before, so all three orders share a line. Also, the header comment says 'In-order' but this file is about post-order.

check.q: In post-order, which value is always printed last?

recap: A binary tree node has a value plus `left` and `right` pointers; `NULL` means no child.
Tree recursion: handle `NULL`, then the node, then the two subtrees.
Pre-order = Root L R, In-order = L Root R, Post-order = L R Root.
Only the position of the print line changes between the three traversals.
Each traversal visits every node once: O(n) time.

check_yourself.q: A tree has root 1, left child 2, right child 3, and 2 has a left child 4. Give all three traversals.

check_yourself.a: Reaching a `NULL` child: the function returns without doing anything.

check_yourself.q: Why is the extra memory O(h) and not O(1)?
check_yourself.a: Each recursive call waits on the call stack, and at most one chain from the root to a leaf (height h) is waiting at a time.
